note: Pass with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the scale was administered in Italian (323 Italian adults, Sapienza Rome). Neither the deposit (S1 File, the study's own SPSS .sav, sha256 2b5e55c9d153acaa41867af83f94c67bb9d686e4d8d50e81a664346ef1c32c9d -- checked at BOTH label levels: all 35 variable labels are None, and the only value labels present are gender {0 Men, 1 Women} and sample {0 students, 1 non-students}) nor the PLOS ONE article carries the Italian item wording; the article's Measures section reproduces exactly one locomotion item, and in English. Base fields therefore hold English, language=Italian, no _translated columns: text_source=translated_substitute. (2) MAPPING: item codes loca1..loca12 are the .sav's own column names, but they carry no wording -- they are positional indices into the RMQ Locomotion scale. Reconstructed from the RMQ's own scoring key (Locomotion = Q1+Q3+Q4+Q5+Q8+(7-Q13)+Q16+Q21+(7-Q24)+Q25+Q28+Q29), which puts the two reverse-worded items at sequence positions 6 and 9 -- exactly where the codes carry their R marker (locaR6, locaR9). Corroborated independently by Ahmadi et al. (2017) Swedish RMQ validation, PMC5702250 Table 3, which enumerates the locomotion items in this same order with (R) on the 6th and 9th. (3) ITEMS ARE STORED ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED. The .sav's own locomotion composite equals the plain unweighted mean of the 12 stored columns with NO reversal applied (max abs diff 0.000 over 323 cases), and Cronbach's alpha on the stored directions is 0.781, matching the paper's published .78 for the total sample, while un-reversing locaR6/locaR9 drops it to 0.582 and pushes exactly those two items to negative item-total correlations. The shipped option anchors for locaR6 and locaR9 are therefore FLIPPED (resp 1 = Strongly Agree, resp 6 = Strongly Disagree) to match the data, following the burkert_2019_whoqol_bref precedent; this is an override of the printed anchor direction and is disclosed here. (4) ANCHORS, ENDS ONLY. The paper states ratings were made on a 6-point scale 'anchored at the ends with 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 6 (Strongly Agree)'. The canonical RMQ form labels all six points (1 strongly disagree, 2 moderately disagree, 3 slightly disagree, 4 slightly agree, 5 moderately agree, 6 strongly agree), but the study's own description outranks it for what this sample saw, so option_text is populated for resp 1 and 6 only and left blank for 2-5 rather than guessed or padded with the level number. (5) TRANSCRIPTION: item_text and instructions are verbatim from the RMQ instrument document, including its typographic apostrophes and quotation marks; only the leading item numbering was stripped. option_text capitalisation follows the paper ('Strongly Disagree'), not the instrument document's lowercase. (6) RIGHTS: no restriction locatable. The RMQ is distributed as a free download with its scoring key from the Society for Judgment and Decision Making's DMIDI inventory (sjdm.org/dmidi/Regulatory_Mode_Questionnaire.html -> files/Kruglanski et al. (2000) RMQ.doc, sha256 b5640f9326759d2a6f33b52f2a1fbcbe4a71318a03f913596f6ffe949cb713d8, fetched 2026-09-10) and is linked for open access from the Kruglanski lab page (terpconnect.umd.edu/~hannahk/Regulatory_Mode.html). Neither page, nor the instrument document itself, states a fee, a permission requirement, a non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. No entry in instrument_rights_register.csv. Silence is permission. (7) Step 3b: the live data is 12 items on a 1-6 scale with R markers at 6 and 9, which is the Locomotion scale and not the 12-item Assessment scale administered alongside it (that one is assR1/ass2../assR11/ass12, with R markers at 1, 5 and 11) nor the 4-item 1-4 self-forgiveness scale. Table name and description are correct. (8) loca5 has only 5 observed resp levels (2-6, no respondent used 1); its row for resp=1 is still emitted because resp=1 is in the table's overall resp set.
